newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent closes up on back of bullish U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent closes up on back of bullish U.S. data.

text.p: IPE Brent closed nine cents higher at $18.13 a barrel on Wednesday, but off firmer levels held for most of the day on the back of bullish U.S. weekly inventory data, traders said.
The June contract hit a high of $18.28 earlier in the day but also traded as low as $18.09. But for most of the late trading June Brent was around the $18.20 mark.

"It's been around these numbers all night and holding firm because every time it went up or down it was following (NYMEX's) WTI which just holding on with gasoline," one broker said. "Gasoline was the market leader".

But traders said that towards the close June Brent suffered a little from a sell-off on NYMEX's WTI contract, which closed three cents down at $19.63. However NYMEX unleaded gasoline contract for June closed 0.59 cents up at 60.90 cents a gallon.

Traders said that June Brent held on firm for most of the day due to the bullish figures from the American Petroleum Institute (API) and the U.S. Department of Energy's Information Administration (EIA).
EIA, which released its data on Wednesday, said gasoline stocks dipped 2.4 million barrels in the May 2 week while API said on Tuesday night that they dipped 3.6 million barrels in the same period.
"The DOE (Department of Energy) draw did not quite confirm the API draw but it was still a good draw," one broker said.

API also stated demand for gasoline was 8.76 million barrels per day, a figure dismissed by some traders as inaccurate but which others said was a record and gave the market a boost. One trader said he expected June Brent to go below $18.00 on Thursday as bullish headline traders in the market had ran out of steam.

"Every time we have seen the market rally, its quite significat that it's done it on very, very low volume so I think we might start to have a look at the downside now. I see it (June Brent) below $18.00 tomorrow," he said.

Earlier, IPE May gas oil futures closed $1.00 higher at $167.50 a tonne, pushed up by mid-afternoon fund buying, brokers said. May hit a high of $168.50 earlier but also slipped to $166.25, or 25 cenbts a tonne below Tuesday's close.
